Play with the tag's colours instead of picking a preset. Choose a shape and three colours; the shading, the shine and the collar's shadow are worked out from each colour, so every combination keeps the same pixel quality. This is also how a pet owner could make the tag their own in the app.

Tag
Collar
Background

Pet
Start from

For customization in the app

  • Curated swatches first, any colour second. Owners pick from a short palette that always looks good; a custom colour is there for anyone who wants an exact match with their pet's real collar.
  • Pick one colour, get three. Each colour you choose becomes a base, a darker shade and a lighter shine, shifted warm and cool like the rest of our pixel art, so a custom tag never looks flat.
  • Guardrails, not rules. If the tag disappears into the background or the paw gets hard to see, a note suggests a fix, such as switching to a light paw, but nothing is blocked.
  • It travels with the pet. The same colours dress the pet's collar and tag in the feed, the diary and the live trip, so the tag a family picks shows up everywhere.

The same necklaces, faces and outfits on every pet, with hats sitting on top of each head. Pick a pet; the choice carries over to Diary deco.

DogsCats

Necklace · 8 options

Today's hanging tag floats two pixels below the collar, which is why it feels off. The others keep everything attached to the head. I'd pick Snug tag as the default (same gold tag, closer) and keep Heart tag for brand moments.

Expressions · 12

The six we have, plus six new ones (peach tiles). Each maps to a moment the sitter's 5-second check or the app can trigger.

Outfits · add-ons only

No hoods, just things that sit cleanly at the neck or on top of the head, so every pet keeps the quality of the original pup.

Tamagotchi sketches after your references 4–6, with every pixel placed by hand on a grid.

Tamagotchi concept · after refs 4–6

A 1-bit pet on an LCD screen that lives through the stay: a baby on pick-up day, grown by the care days, and the icons around the screen are the sitter's actions (meal, walk, bath, meds, nap, photo). When the sitter taps one, the owner's pet does it too.

Growing up · cream screen
Dark LCD · after ref 5
Icon set · after ref 6 · 16 × 16, 1-pixel line

The screens blink every couple of seconds (it stays still with Reduce motion). Everything here is a sketch to choose from; tell me which direction to take and I'll polish it and make the masters.

An idea, not a logo file: an outfit layer for the pixel pets, inspired by Duolingo's suit events (quests unlock some, a shop sells others) and Pokémon Unite's seasonal holowear (themed sets, rarity colours). Every costume below is real pixel art on the same 24-pixel pets, so it's ready to try.

Where it fits

  • The pet's avatar on Home, in the daily note, the four-cut strip and stickers.
  • Rewards for care, not purchases: first stay, reading notes, leaving a review.
  • Seasons Korean owners already celebrate: Chuseok, Halloween, Christmas, the pet's birthday.

Why it's worth it

  • Owners come back between stays to see what their pet is wearing.
  • It turns the sitter's update into something shareable: a costumed four-cut is made for Instagram.
  • It fits "learn without asking": the outfit itself says it rained, or it's a birthday.

Watch out

  • Scope: it's after the 5-stage demo (P2). A single Halloween moment could be a small demo extra.
  • Tone: no pay-to-win and no streak guilt; this is a care app.
  • Respect: cultural outfits like saekdong and hanbok should feel celebratory, not like a joke.

Sketch 1 · The Closet

The suit-event layout adapted: a seasonal banner with a countdown, Stay quests that unlock outfits by caring (first stay, reading 7 notes, a review), and a Season row. Instead of a price, an owner can ask the sitter for an outfit at booking, which is a nice excuse for a dress-up photo. Rarity uses pastel tiles (Common mint, Rare sky, Epic lilac) rather than loud game colours.

Sketch 2 · It dresses for the day

The strongest use is context, not cosmetics. The avatar puts on an outfit by itself when something happens, so the owner gets the news at a glance.

Sketch 3 · The wardrobe

Nine outfits, each drawn as a layer over any pet: hoods hide the ears, hats sit on top, collars replace the green one. Shown on the golden pup and the orange tabby.
